items.answer: Geothermal drilling consists of drilling vertical boreholes to install closed-loop geothermal probes. These probes, made from durable synthetic materials, contain a heat-transfer fluid (water or a mixture of water and monopropylene glycol) that circulates in a closed loop. This fluid extracts heat from the ground and transfers it to your heat pump system. The length and depth of the boreholes are calculated when sizing the system, in order to optimise energy efficiency.
items.question: What does closed-loop geothermal drilling involve?

items.answer: Vertical geothermal boreholes require little space and are not affected by weather conditions. Indeed, beyond a certain depth the ground temperature stays constant. The extracted heat therefore remains stable in every season, even in severe cold. Moreover, because they use a renewable energy source, these systems are economical and environmentally friendly.
items.question: What are the benefits of vertical geothermal boreholes?

items.answer: In addition to heating your home, geothermal energy can also cool your spaces during the summer months, thanks to the principle of natural or passive cooling. This process uses the constant temperature of the ground to lower your building's temperature without intensive use of your heat pump. The indoor heat of your home is captured and transferred to the cooler ground, cooling your rooms.
items.question: How does closed-loop geothermal cooling of a home work?

items.answer: A traditional air conditioning system consumes a lot of electricity and uses chemical refrigerants. Geothermal cooling, by contrast, is a natural and silent solution that reduces your energy consumption while ensuring optimal thermal comfort. This environmentally friendly approach lets you keep a pleasant temperature at home even during heatwaves.
items.question: What are the benefits of closed-loop geothermal cooling?

items.answer: The depth of the geothermal borehole is defined when sizing your installation. The closed-loop geothermal boreholes drilled by WellDoneDrill typically reach a depth between 100 and 200 metres, depending on your building's energy needs and the local geology.
items.question: What is the depth of a closed-loop geothermal borehole?

items.answer: A geothermal heat pump offers excellent energy efficiency: for 1 kWh of electricity consumed, it can produce on average 4 to 6 kWh of heat. This means that up to 80% of the energy used to heat your home comes for free from the ground, while only 20% comes from the electricity needed to run the system.
